chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥammād and al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, all together from al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no deceased person who dies and is left alone except that Shaytan plays within his interior.”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, said: And a piece of iron should not be left upon his abdomen, as the common people do. We heard that in discussion from the shuyukh, may Allah have mercy upon them.

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: Then preparation should be made for his ghusl (ritual bath). So one ratl of ground lote leaves is taken, and about that amount of ushnaan, a small amount with which cleansing is done, and of fine camphor half a mithqal, if available; otherwise whatever is available of it, even if little; and of pure dharīrah, from the well-known perfume called al-qumḥah, an amount of one ratl or more than that. We shall mention this when explaining the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased and his shrouding, if Allah Most High wills.

Then he said: And for his ḥunūṭ, there should be taken the weight of thirteen dirhams and one-third of raw camphor that has not been touched by fire, and that is the proper amount for ḥunūṭ. Its moderate amount is the weight of four dirhams, and its minimum is the weight of one mithqal, unless that is not possible.

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: ground lote leaves used in preparing the washing of the deceased
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Shaytan, mentioned here in relation to the deceased being left alone
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in the rites of the deceased, especially ḥunūṭ
key_terms.تَكْفِينِهِ: his shrouding in the funeral process
key_terms.غُسْلِهِ: his ghusl (ritual bath), meaning the washing of the deceased
key_terms.لِحَنُوطِهِ: for his ḥunūṭ, the application of camphor to the deceased
key_terms.مَيِّتٍ: a deceased person whose body is being discussed in funeral rulings
key_terms.مِثْقَالٍ: a unit of weight used for measuring funerary substances

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about leaving the deceased alone and preparing camphor and other materials for the deceased’s ghusl (ritual bath) and ḥunūṭ?
ai.summary: This report and the accompanying statement of al-Shaykh discuss rulings and practices concerning the deceased immediately after death, including not leaving the body alone and preparing materials for ghusl (ritual bath), takfīn, and ḥunūṭ. It reflects Shia legal guidance on funerary care, while also indicating the discouragement of certain common practices not established in the tradition.
